>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump is touting the construction of a steel mill in Iowa that he says has tariffs
made possible.
Iowa has closely watched House and Senate races with control of Congress at stake this
year.
NPR's Deepa Shivram reports that the plant is expected to create about 2,000 jobs but
not expected to begin producing steel until 2030.
>> Trump's announcement comes as Americans are souring on how they view Trump's handling

And with the midterm elections just a little over a month away, the president is running

>> Today we're thrilled to announce that Massabi Metallics will be building the largest steel

It's the largest plant, one of the largest plants in the world.
>> The steel plant is being built by Massabi Metallics, a company based in Minnesota, though
the plant will be constructed in Iowa.

The $15 billion investment marks the first mega steel plant to be built in the US since

Deepa Shivram, NPR News, the White House.
>> Now to the UK, where five British nationals described as terrorist suspects have been released
on bail.
They were detained yesterday near a British military base used by the US to launch strikes
on Iran.
That location prompted concerns about a connection to the Middle East, as NPR's Lauren Freya
reports.
>> British counter-terrorism officials say the men are still under investigation for
explosives and terrorism offenses, and that authorities are investigating multiple lines
of inquiry, including whether the suspects were working for Iran, Russia, or other non-state
groups, quote, knowingly or unknowingly.
Iran's embassy in London denies any involvement, saying malicious speculation only fuels Iran's
ronophobia.
The men, Londoners, all in their mid-20s, were detained in the middle of the night near
RAF Royal Air Force Base, Fairford, west of London.
It's been the target of anti-war protestors as well.
Lauren Freya, NPR News, London.
>> Prosecutors say they're reopening an investigation into alleged sexual assault by members of the
CHI-5 fraternity at Cornell University.
Aurora Berry of member station WSKG reports that it's after a public uproar following
a lawsuit against the university, several Greek life organizations, and fraternity members.
>> The plaintiff in the lawsuit was a Cornell student at the time of the incident.
The lawsuit says she was drugged and sexually assaulted by seven fraternity members in 2024.
Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten says the plaintiff, quote, "did
not allege that she was drugged against her will or gang-raped" in her original statement.
Van Houten says the case will now go before a grand jury.
Cornell's vice president for university relations, Kyle Kimball, says that the university supports
the decision to reopen the investigation.
The lawsuit says Cornell didn't do enough to protect the plaintiff.
For NPR News, I'm Aurora Berry in Ithaca.
>> This is NPR News.
The US Senate has passed a bipartisan bill that would regulate college sports, a measure
passed this evening on a 77 to 22 vote.
It would codify into law the settlement of a 2025 lawsuit that allowed colleges to pay
players who would also establish new guardrails a bill faces an uncertain future in the house.

from Ocean State Media reports.
>> The nor'easter walloped the region with heavy rains and winds clocked as high as 70
miles per hour in New York City.
One Brooklyn man who worked for the City Housing Authority was struck and killed by a falling
tree.
On the town's on the Jersey Shore, the water was waist deep.
At the height of the storm, 180,000 customers in New Jersey alone lost power.
Work crews were busy all weekend long and most of the outages have been restored.
On Nantucket, the storm deposited a huge chunk of a shipwreck onto the beach.
It may be part of a three-masted schooner that sank in 1884.
For NPR News, I'm David Wright in Greenport, New York.
>> Forecasters say Hurricane Polo is nearing landfall on Mexico's Baja California Peninsula.

Further west, forecasters say Hurricane Nolo is edging away from the main Hawaiian Islands
